stem: Which do-it-yourself technique corrects readout error in raw SamplerV2 counts?

options.text: Solve against an assignment (confusion) matrix measured from calibration circuits, e.g. with M3
Raise `sampler.options.resilience_level` until the readout error is mitigated away
Apply Zero-Noise Extrapolation to the returned bitstrings, extrapolating each shot to the zero-noise limit
Enable gate twirling, which measures and then inverts the readout confusion matrix for you
Apply Probabilistic Error Cancellation to the counts, inverting the learned noise channel shot by shot
Fit the histogram to a maximum-likelihood estimate of the ideal distribution, with no calibration run

explanation.correct: Readout error acts as a classical channel on the measured bits: an assignment (confusion) matrix M, measured with calibration circuits (prepare each basis state, record what is read back), maps the true distribution to the observed one. Solving that linear system for the true distribution corrects the counts (in practice not by explicit inversion; M3 solves a much smaller system restricted to the bitstrings actually observed). The Sampler's raw per-shot data is exactly the input this needs, so you do it in post-processing: the Sampler's own noise-management options are dynamical decoupling and Pauli twirling only.

distractors.B: SamplerV2 has no `resilience_level` (0.48: assigning it raises a ValidationError), and a resilience level would not build a readout-calibration matrix in any case. The primitives guide's remark that the IBM primitives include error mitigation refers to the Estimator; the Sampler offers no built-in mitigation.
distractors.C: Zero-Noise Extrapolation mitigates *expectation values* by amplifying gate noise and extrapolating; it is not defined on individual sampled bitstrings.
distractors.D: Gate twirling randomizes two-qubit gate noise and never touches the readout. Even measurement twirling only diagonalizes the readout-error transfer matrix; the calibration and rescaling built on it (TREX) is an Estimator expectation-value step, not something the Sampler applies to counts.
distractors.E: PEC is an expectation-value technique: it reweights sampled circuits with signed quasi-probabilities, which cannot be applied to individual bitstrings. Readout correction on counts is a confusion-matrix problem.
distractors.F: Without calibration data nothing tells the fit what the device's readout error looks like. Constrained fits of this kind (minimizing ||M p - p_obs|| with p non-negative) still need a measured assignment matrix M.

provenance.notes: s5 adversarial review: high-severity length tell fixed; resilience ruling: distractor B names resilience_level as Estimator-only; added the Sampler noise-management guide as the authoritative citation for the DD/twirling-only option set | pool wave: +E PEC on bitstrings, +F calibration-free MLE | realism audit 2026-10-01: stem trimmed from 37 words; re-rated 3->2; M3 Sampler tutorial added as citation | adversarial A3 2026-10-16: DF falsely called M3 a maximum-likelihood fit (readout tutorial: M3 solves p~ = M p on a reduced matrix; 'equation (2) is not solved by inverting M') -> DF/correct/key text say 'solve against' the assignment matrix; 'rigorously' dropped from stem (M3 neglects 3rd-order correlations); docs traps answered: primitives guide 'SamplerV2 ... including error mitigation' (DB), error-mitigation 'measurement twirling ... diagonalizing the readout-error transfer matrix' (DD, TREX is Estimator); primitives citation (no readout content) dropped
